question.text: Mr. Arjun Sethi, an anchor investor in 'Ganga Venture Partners AIF', wants copies of Contribution Agreements signed by other investors to check comparable terms. The manager's stance should be:

answer.text: Share all Contribution Agreements transparently since they are public documents
The Contribution Agreement for each Contributor is generally NOT shared with other Contributors, as it contains representations and warranties specific to each Contributor
Share only Contribution Agreements of Indian investors, not foreign ones
Share Contribution Agreements only after redacting the investor's name

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 13.4, the Contribution Agreement for each Contributor is generally not shared with other Contributors because it contains representations and warranties specific to each Contributor (such as source of funds, accreditation, regulatory status, tax status, etc.). Confidentiality is inherent to the bilateral nature of the agreement. The Trap: Transparency is desirable but confidentiality of investor-specific reps and warranties trumps. An MFN clause (not sharing the full agreement) is the standard mechanism to address parity concerns. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B tests disclosure obligations under PPM. XIX-C requires distinguishing PPM (shared with all) vs Contribution Agreement (bilateral, confidential) vs Trust Deed (shared with all). Manager's Pro-Tip: Instead of sharing agreements, negotiate an MFN clause upfront for key LPs — but carve out exceptions for terms tied to ticket size, jurisdiction, or regulatory status to preserve flexibility.
